structure:
Teach in the Spirit Island order: overview, setup, a round in play order, then reference. Proposed book:
PART 1, LEARN TO PLAY. (1) The game in brief: story, win and lose, the Discord deck as the clock, "you always see what's coming", and team choices with a tie-break (earliest in player order decides). (2) Components: §2's piece table plus pictures and the four card-token types. (3) The map: hexes, sites with three states (neutral, yours, corrupted) and blocking, reach, fronts. This is the only rule-heavy part before setup. (4) Setup, with difficulty and player count folded in as step 0, using a per-count setup card (bases, start hexes, home cities, board order, tip size). (5) Unity and Discord: sway, holding Discord off, tipping. It moves up because it is checked after every action. (6) Your AI board and resources: §5 and §6 merged. Insight goes here. Powers sit on the boards, not in the text. Node tracks and sacrifice stay in the text. (7) The round at a glance (the table). Then one short section per step, in play order: A Sway; B the adversary's turn (event, threats dealt, rally, deploy, other lines, projects and botnets in one paragraph, overrun and Corrupt X, march, reveal and income); C cards (opening, build, draft, keep, playing a card, tags, buildings); D the action phase (standard actions, then ambassadors: move, claim and liberate as one comparison table, remove agents, the cancel rule); E production (one list, which absorbs "When income arrives", megaprojects and converters); F threats (near against nearest, countering); G war; H cleanup. (8) Protecting your pieces: the destruction list, guarding, last-node table, markers. Merge §9 Guarding, §13 Destruction and Losing nodes, and the War node rule here.
PART 2, REFERENCE. The full Corrupt X procedure, location-token rules, Rally edge cases, corp-troop and ambassador cases, projects and slot fitting, Unity/Discord prohibitions, the difficulty card (one table), solo, the card legend (§18, slimmed to what icons carry), glossary with page numbers, and a back-cover round summary.
Merges and moves: §5+§6. §9 split three ways: Claim, Liberate, Remove and Move go to the action phase; Blocking goes to the map; Gather, Push, Strike, Convert and Firewall go to the legend. §13 split: the march goes to the adversary's turn, corp troops to the war step and tipping, destruction to Protecting your pieces. §15 goes into §1 plus the purge table printed on the Unity track. §16+§17 become setup and reference cards. Megaproject text from §8 and §12 becomes one section. Delete the repeats: Sell (3 places), Move (2), claim and liberate costs (2), guarding (2), blocking (3), corp-troop protection (2), last node (3), arrival cancel (2), Garrisons (adversary board and difficulty table). Cut the designer notes: the front matter, "poor value on purpose", "never by one player's reach", "the rules call this a strike". Fix the cards rather than decode them ("each board" means each country). Then the core text loses about a quarter of its words with no rule changed.
worked_examples: Corruption on a small board fragment: two cities share neighbor hexes, a Corrupt Cities line runs in hex order, each city takes just enough agents from next door (lowest-numbered first), one city's marker counts as an agent, and the second city fails because the first took its agents. Then the node on the corrupted city is destroyed and the ambassador there is removed.

A round-2 card turn for the Researcher: build a hand of 4 (tier 1 or 2, face up), draft with passing, keep two cards with the Science discount on the tier-2 keep, run out of insight and pay 5 credits for the last keep, then play a card with what is left. It shows that keeps and plays draw on the same insight.

Block, then liberate, then claim: Move puts two ambassadors on a corrupted city over two rounds (no Discord diverted, and an arriving rally agent cancels one). Liberate costs 5 + agents; the standing ambassadors pay first and your supply pays the rest. Sway 5 Unity and decide how much holds Discord off. The city turns neutral, and a nearby botnet now blocks the claim.
Placing a node: Deploy (1 energy) plus the track space's energy (economy space 4 = 1 more), what the uncovered space gives, where the node may go (agents fine, marker not), and how reach grows.

A threat from deal to effect: the event's pull, turning up cards until the tag and location fit, the token on the place with the most adversary pieces nearby, who is near (pays) against who is nearest (is hit), two players pooling credits, a partial payment refunded when it goes unpaid, and the harm landing on the nearest player.

An adversary troop's march: two steps, a move then a strike on a player factory. Wall makes the troop walk around the Protector's node. A corp troop at the base next door is removed instead of the factory, and a second troop meets a hardening token. Show Vigil firing.

A Discord tip at 3 players: the track reaches 9, the tip count goes to 3 (tier II), the track empties, neutral factories feed corp troops to their bases (an ambassador on one factory stops it), the Discord card resolves, and at round end war on a front destroys a factory with a node on it.

Production for one player in one round, in order: factory chips, a city building a factory on an adjacent zone, buying a neutral city's energy for 5 credits, station cubes completing a megaproject and every cube paying out, an agent on a bare node hex costing insight next round, then upkeep.

friction.rule: Garrisons against the difficulty table's agent income
friction.hard: §10 lists Garrisons as +1 agent income, but the §16 table's agent income (1/4/4/4/3) already includes it, as does setup's "1 a country". A reader adds it twice: the pool is wrong from setup on.
friction.change: Mark the column "includes Garrisons", or list the base figure and the board's +1 apart.

friction.hard: Two corruption counts run every round: Corrupt X counts on and next to the site and pulls agents in; natural corruption counts the site's own hex only. Same corrupt numbers, same marker rule, different reach, steps 9 and 10 back to back.
friction.change: Name natural corruption apart ("overrun"), teach it first as the base rule, then Corrupt X as "also pulls from next door". Rule fix: one count for both.

friction.rule: Simultaneous action phase and team choices
friction.hard: All players act at once, but nothing says what happens when order matters (two players want the last ambassador slot, the same converter, a threat's last payment), or when the players disagree on a team choice. The engine resolves it some fixed way; the book doesn't say which.
friction.change: One general line early: "When order matters or players disagree, the earliest player in player order decides." This states the engine's order without changing it.

friction.rule: Liberate gives the site to nobody
friction.hard: A player expects to take the site they liberate. It turns neutral, and claiming it is a second action, which an adjacent botnet that didn't stop the liberation now forbids.
friction.change: Lead the Liberate rule with "the site turns neutral; claim it to own it" and teach it in the block-liberate-claim example. Only a rule change could make Liberate own the site.

friction.hard: Five words for three states (neutral/clean, owned/aligned, corrupted), plus dark (an agent on a city) and blocked, plus "home city". The table uses two names per cell.
friction.change: Use neutral, yours and corrupted only. Write "blocked" for any site with an opposing piece. Drop clean, aligned and dark.

friction.hard: A house meaning against the English one, used in dozens of rules. Strike then uses "adjacent" to mean the opposite, and readers miss which is which.
friction.change: Write "on or next to" in full wherever it is meant, so "next to" keeps its English sense.

friction.rule: Playable card with nothing to act on
friction.hard: The heading says nothing blocks a card, and the last sentence says a card doing nothing can't be played.
friction.change: "Play a card if any part can act; skip parts that can't."

friction.rule: Draft direction by player order, not seating
friction.hard: Player order is set by board (Builder, Protector, Researcher), and hands pass to the next and previous player. Unless players sit in player order, passing at the table breaks.
friction.change: Setup: sit in player order. Combine with #31's arrow on the round track.

friction.hard: The board table's "Income each round" includes 5 insight, but insight is set at round start, not paid in upkeep, and the real start value is 6 (first track space).
friction.change: Move insight to its own column, "insight each round", and print 6.

friction.hard: Every player meets it every round, in every keep and play decision: reset, carry for the Researcher (own but not gifted), debt from last round, credits for keeps but not plays, three keep regimes.
friction.change: Rank 3. Rewording does half the job (print 6, insight-loss tokens, one keep table). The rest needs a rule change: one keep price all game.

friction.hard: As written; now also the second count from natural corruption (new entry).
friction.change: Keep at 1.

friction.hard: As written.
friction.change: Rank 4.

friction.hard: As written, plus the new liberate-to-neutral entry.

top_ten: Garrisons is printed on the adversary board and is already inside the difficulty table's agent income, so a reader adds it twice from setup on. Say "includes Garrisons".
Teach Unity/Discord (sway, hold-off, tip) before the round walkthrough: it is checked after every action, and the Discord deck is the game's clock. Put that in §1.
Corruption is two different counts every round (natural: on the hex; Corrupt X: on and next to, with pulls). Name them apart and teach both with one worked board fragment.
Merge Claim and Liberate into one comparison table, and lead Liberate with "the site turns neutral, not yours"; teach block, liberate, claim as one example.
One numbered production list absorbs "When income arrives", cities' energy, station output and megaprojects; print each site's output by owner color on the board.
Add the missing general rule for simultaneous play and team choices: when order matters or players disagree, the earliest in player order decides (state what the engine does).

Cut the duplicates (Sell ×3, guarding ×2, blocking ×3, last node ×3, Move ×2, corp-troop protection ×2, the arrival cancel ×2). Cut the designer notes ("poor value on purpose", "the rules call this a strike", "each board means each country": fix the card instead).

Move powers, capstones, converters, event lines, Liberate/Convert/Gather/Strike/Firewall wording to the boards, cards and legend. The core book teaches sacrifice, node tracks and the card grammar only.
Use three site-state words (neutral, yours, corrupted) plus "blocked". Always write "adversary troop" or "corp troop" in full. Write "on or next to" wherever it is meant.

Rerank friction by reader cost: Insight+Keeps up to 3, production timing to 7, words-with-two-meanings to 10, factory growth to 12. Destruction and last-node go down, Wall goes down (one player). Liberate cards is engine fault M1, not a design entry: fix the engine to the documented rule.
